note: Dimension matrix built only for the sources that ground the paper's Gap (the competing/prior benchmarks). Dataset- and model-provenance citations (CIFAR-10, MobileNet, ResNet, Speech Commands, MSCOCO, ToyADMOS, DCASE2020, MIMII, 80M Tiny Images, TFLM, RISC-V, MicroNets, SpArSe, the LoRa energy-cost source) are method/attribution citations, not competing approaches, so they are not rows in this gap-grounding matrix; they are used directly in Methods with their role stated in source_registry.json.

matrix.problem_framing: Benchmark raw MCU compute performance with a simple, portable, easy-to-implement test.
matrix.method_family: Fixed-algorithm micro-benchmark (e.g. list processing, matrix manipulation, CRC) run to completion, scored as iterations/second.
matrix.key_assumption: A handful of representative general-purpose algorithms is a sufficient proxy for MCU performance.
matrix.data_eval: No dataset; synthetic workloads baked into the benchmark code.
matrix.strength: Extremely easy to port and run; became the de facto standard for comparing MCU-class chips.
matrix.weakness_limit: Does not profile a full program, and its workloads are not representative of ML inference (per MLPerf Tiny's own characterization, E020).
matrix.relation_to_us: Shows MCU-class performance comparison is a solved, adopted problem in general -- but not for ML workloads specifically; motivates why a new suite, not just CoreMark, is needed.

matrix.problem_framing: Benchmark actual ML inference workloads across edge-class devices and frameworks.
matrix.method_family: Runs full trained ML models (image classification/detection) end-to-end on candidate hardware.
matrix.key_assumption: Edge devices have enough memory/runtime budget to host the chosen reference models.
matrix.strength: First move from synthetic micro-benchmarking (CoreMark) to real ML workloads on real hardware.
matrix.weakness_limit: Reference models need gigabytes of memory and have significant runtimes -- too large for MCU-class devices; no power measurement support (E021).
matrix.relation_to_us: Shows real-workload ML benchmarking is possible, but not yet at MCU scale or with power as a first-class metric -- the two properties MLPerf Tiny adds.

matrix.problem_framing: Community-driven, industry-standard benchmarking of ML inference across a broad range of systems.
matrix.method_family: A suite of reference ML models and rules for submitting inference results, with (planned) power measurement.
matrix.key_assumption: Compatible implementations and 'small' benchmarks are not the primary need -- the suite targets larger-scale inference systems first.
matrix.data_eval: Standard-scale ML models and datasets (server/mobile class).
matrix.strength: Broad industry adoption and governance model (a template MLPerf Tiny explicitly follows for submissions/review, E009); plans to add power.
matrix.weakness_limit: Currently precludes MCUs and other resource-constrained platforms for lack of small benchmarks and compatible implementations (E022).
matrix.relation_to_us: Establishes the submission/review governance pattern MLPerf Tiny reuses (E009), while MLPerf Tiny fills the MCU-scale gap this suite explicitly does not yet cover.

lit_gap_chain_pointer: See story/lit_gap_chain.md for the assembled Literature -> Gap -> Question chain built from this matrix.
